gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Noto Sans Elymaic keeps its apertures wide and its ascenders low. Unica One above it is all pencil-line consistency with big open eyes, so a large heading and modest body text would sit comfortably together.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Neon tubing bent into letters is the best way to picture Unica One. It commands attention with constant-thickness strokes, while Noto Sans Ethiopic does the quieter job of staying sturdy and tall, with terminals hanging far from the bowl.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Unica One lays down bars of identical thickness, line after line, with a very large lowercase eye. Noto Sans Georgian follows with open curves and short ascender stems, and a larger heading next to smaller text would make the gap obvious.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-glagolitic: Unica One draws its letters without any pressure swells, so the eye never slows down inside a curve. Noto Sans Glagolitic then fills the page with open round forms and a tall, sturdy lowercase that stay clear at small sizes.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Lowercase counters as big as drilled glass beads give Noto Sans Gothic an open, parenthesis-round look. And Unica One answers with strokes that never swell or thin, a commanding stiffness against all that roundness.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Each stroke in Unica One is as stout as a drawn pipe cleaner. It is the one to grab attention with its big lowercase eye, whereas Noto Sans Grantha quietly keeps a read smooth, its tall little bowls never snagging.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Distinctive from the first line, Unica One has no calligraphic modulation at all and looks best big and short. Noto Sans Gujarati takes over with curved strokes that end before turning inward, and large open counters in a, e and s.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-go: Bold tubes, wide-open eyes, zero fuss. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi supplies lowercase strokes as tall as a thick crayon mark, and its terminals cut back to leave big gaps that soften the heading's horizontals, exactly as heavy as its verticals.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Noto Sans Gurmukhi points its terminals outward like a pair of tongs. Unica One brings tubular strokes like bent copper pipe, and that metallic uniformity is the strongest thing about the pair against the low-slung ascenders below.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Contemporary in feel, Unica One frames its counters with strokes of the same width, and that is where it does its best work. Noto Sans Hanunoo does the reading, with lowercase filling most of the height and terminals that stay open.
